rationale:
Round-2 critique: I accept most of it and revert to the raced design, changing one variable.

Accepted: (1) The footprint explanation is weak. Line loss needs the summed readings below 0.05, which only happens when all sensors are almost off the tape, at about the 0.06 m off-track limit. A larger footprint therefore cannot prevent the early loss on its own. (2) The revision changed six things at once, so its race could not test the footprint. (3) The kp reduction (3.0 to 2.5) and the speed reduction (1.7 to 1.6) have no supporting evidence. The critique is right that they work against correcting drift and against the 3 s completion limit. I restore kp 3.0 and base_speed 1.7. (4) The ki and kd values rest on rough estimates, so I keep the raced values (ki 0.3, kd 0.1) rather than adjusting them on unmeasured bounds.

Rejected: I keep the sensor span at x = +/-0.03 rather than widening it. The critique is right that widening the span changes the signal gain, and I have no evidence either way. I keep line_loss last_direction. search_left and stop would also need evidence, and only one design races per iteration.

What I changed: only the sensor footprint, from 12 mm to 16 mm. The 15 mm pitch then gives full, gap-free coverage of the tape across the array, instead of 3 mm gaps. This is a single-variable test of whether sensor coverage affects line-loss events and progress. Mass, body length and all controller values match the raced iteration-0 design, so any change in results can be attributed to the footprint.

Decision rule for the next race: if progress or line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom tracks improves over the raced design (progress above 0.16 or line_loss below 1), keep the 16 mm footprint. If not, revert to 12 mm. Completion is still the main test, and the 3 s limit remains untested.

Expected results (hypotheses, not data): a modest change in progress and line_loss_events at most. Completion is unlikely with this single change, and the design does not address tracking-error growth directly. Main risk: the raced failure mode, lateral error growth to the 0.06 m limit, is unchanged.
